Join Laboratory to Patient on patient ID and count the lab test records for each distinct SEX value in Patient. Treat any blank or NULL SEX as its own group. Compute the average count per sex group. For each sex whose count is above that average, show the sex, its count, its share of the total joined records, and how far above the average it is as a relative percentage ((count - average) / average * 100), unrounded.
queries:
WITH g AS (
  SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(P.SEX), ''), 'UNKNOWN') AS sex, COUNT(*) AS cnt
  FROM Laboratory L
  JOIN Patient P ON L.ID = P.ID
  GROUP BY COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(P.SEX), ''), 'UNKNOWN')
),
t AS (
  SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt, SUM(cnt) AS total FROM g
)
SELECT g.sex,
       g.cnt,
       g.cnt * 1.0 / t.total AS share,
       g.cnt - t.avg_cnt AS diff
FROM g, t
WHERE g.cnt > t.avg_cnt;
WITH sex_counts AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(P.SEX), ''), 'Unknown') AS sex_group,
           COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM Laboratory L
    JOIN Patient P ON L.ID = P.ID
    GROUP BY COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(P.SEX), ''), 'Unknown')
),
stats AS (
    SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) AS avg_cnt, SUM(cnt) AS total_cnt
    FROM sex_counts
)
SELECT sc.sex_group AS SEX,
       sc.cnt AS count,
       sc.cnt * 1.0 / s.total_cnt AS share_of_total,
       (sc.cnt - s.avg_cnt) / s.avg_cnt * 100 AS pct_above_average
FROM sex_counts sc
CROSS JOIN stats s
WHERE sc.cnt > s.avg_cnt;
